1933: The Nationalist Pivot
The Decision
At the 1933 London Economic Conference, FDR intentionally
torpedoed international efforts to stabilize global currencies.
The Rationale
To save the American domestic economy from deflation, FDR
abandoned the gold-standard orthodoxy. He recognized
that U.S. national self-interest (raising domestic prices and
wages) was fundamentally incompatible with acting as a
responsible global creditor.
The Legacy
This calculated economic isolationism established the
blueprint for modern U.S. policy: domestic imperatives will
always overrule international financial stability.
